--- title: "Pseudoword reading: three syllables" subtitle: "Automatically generated task sheet · LEC_PSEUDO_3sil" --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} **Automatically generated task sheet** (C · Oral reading fluency; quality class A). Generated on November 27, 2026 with `scripts/R/ficha_generica_v3.R --tarea LEC_PSEUDO_3sil`. Figures come from the data; the theoretical framework is shared by the tasks of the same construct. **Interpretation and team review are missing.** Spanish name: *Lectura de pseudopalabras trisílabas*. [Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/auto/LEC_PSEUDO_3sil.html). ::: **In one sentence.** Pseudoword reading: three syllables, from age 6 to 8 (8,513 administrations in 3 cohorts; 2 forms). Stability across time points ρ = .65. AUC .86–.92 against persistent difficulty (circular: the label uses this task). ## Description | | | |---|---| | Codes | 1935 76 | | Battery | DIS-ESP | | Format | reading aloud | | Items | 12 (1935) according to the platform | | Task family | C · Oral reading fluency | | Score | Correct responses per minute | | Instructions (platform) | The child is asked to read as quick and accurately as possible lists of 12 words/pseudowords increasing length (2, 3, and 4 syllables) presented on the screen. Correct responses and time are recorded. | ## How it is programmed on the platform The platform is the reference: what the activity actually presents is what is measured. Configuration read from the activity itself on 23/10/2026 (without modifying it). Cell contents are in Spanish. | Code|Name on the platform |Presentation | Test items| Practice items|Example items |Time limit |Order |Scoring | Age.term (label 3)| |----:|:-------------------------|:--------------------------|----------:|--------------:|:-------------|:----------|:---------|:----------|-------------------------------------------:| | 1935|Pseudopalabras trisílabas |Lista de ítems en pantalla | 12| 0|— |— |aleatorio |Eficiencia | 6.1, 6.2, 6.3, 7.1, 7.2, 7.3, 8.1, 8.2, 8.3| *Age.term: provisional reading of the activity's label 3 (3rd digit = age, 4th = term; 0 = annual), to be confirmed with the engineer.* **How it looks on the platform** (first item or example; 2026 screenshot; the interface is in Spanish). For the reading lists only the first two items are shown. ::: {layout-ncol=1} ![1935 · Pseudopalabras trisílabas](../../figuras/plataforma/1935.jpg){.lightbox width="40%" fig-alt="Screenshot of activity 1935"} ::: ## Theoretical framework Reading syllables, words and pseudowords aloud measures **written word recognition**: converting letters into sounds and accessing the word. It is the decoding component of the simple view of reading [@hoover1990simple] and the core of dyslexia according to the IDA definition (@sec-definicion). **What distinguishes each list.** Dual-route models separate two procedures. The **sublexical route** converts graphemes into phonemes and is the only one that works for pseudowords. The **lexical route** recognizes the whole word, and it shows in words being read faster than pseudowords (lexicality effect) and frequent words faster than rare ones. In Spanish, children use both from Grade 2 [@avdyli2014lexical; @davies2013lexical]. That is why the platform has both lists: pseudowords measure pure decoding, and the difference with words estimates how much orthographic lexicon the child has built. Length (from one to four syllables) makes serial reading visible: the more the child depends on letter-by-letter conversion, the more each added syllable costs. **In a transparent orthography, what discriminates is speed.** In Spanish, almost all children read accurately by the middle of Grade 1. Children with dyslexia are accurate but read more slowly, and their reading resembles that of younger children of the same reading level: it is delayed rather than deviant development [@davies2007spanish]. A meta-analysis of 79 European studies concludes that reading speed distinguishes readers with dyslexia in all orthographies and ages, whereas accuracy depends on age and transparency [@carioti2021depth]. In German, 70% of slow readers in Grade 1 were still slow in Year 8 [@landerl2008fluency]. That is why the score in these task sheets is **correct responses per minute**, not correct responses. **What our data show.** These are the most reliable and valid tasks on the platform: - **Reliability.** Stability between terms of ρ = .65 to .81, and 2021 α between .73 and .97. - **External validity.** They predict low Woodcock-Muñoz reading fluency years later with a median AUC of .72 to .77 ([chapter](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/criterio-woodcock.html), *in Spanish*). The longer lists (three- and four-syllable words) predict best. - **Delay or deviance.** Comparing pseudowords with words among children of the same reading level separates delay from deviance ([Norms by reading level](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/baremo-nivel-lector.html), *in Spanish*). ## Sample and descriptive statistics | Time point| Form| Cohort| Session|School year | N| Non-Preleo| Preleo| Schools| |----------:|----:|------:|-------:|:-----------|---:|----------:|------:|-------:| | 6.2| 1935| 2011| 188|2017/18 | 723| 0| 723| 30| | 6.3| 76| 2010| 160|2016/17 | 915| 252| 662| 34| | 6.3| 1935| 2011| 193|2017/18 | 663| 0| 663| 30| | 6.3| 76| 2012| 634|2018/19 | 328| 325| 0| 16| | 7.1| 1935| 2010| 184|2017/18 | 790| 253| 536| 31| | 7.1| 1935| 2011| 635|2018/19 | 565| 0| 565| 25| | 7.1| 1935| 2012| 899|2019/20 | 208| 204| 0| 14| | 7.2| 1935| 2010| 189|2017/18 | 801| 248| 552| 31| | 7.2| 1935| 2011| 636|2018/19 | 543| 0| 543| 25| | 7.2| 1935| 2012| 904|2019/20 | 219| 215| 0| 11| | 7.3| 1935| 2010| 190|2017/18 | 421| 163| 258| 30| | 7.3| 3934| 2011| 637|2018/19 | 500| 0| 500| 24| | 8.1| 1935| 2010| 638|2018/19 | 543| 165| 377| 25| | 8.1| 1935| 2011| 900|2019/20 | 393| 0| 393| 25| | 8.2| 1935| 2011| 905|2019/20 | 429| 0| 429| 22| | 8.3| 1935| 2010| 640|2018/19 | 472| 112| 359| 24| | Form| Time point| N| Cohorts| Mean| SD| Median| Skewness|% floor |% ceiling | |----:|----------:|---:|----------:|-----:|-----:|------:|--------:|:-------|:---------| | 76| 6.3| 577| 2010, 2012| 16.74| 7.58| 17.10| -0.20|NA |NA | | 1935| 7.1| 457| 2010, 2012| 18.54| 7.79| 18.23| 0.24|NA |NA | | 1935| 7.2| 463| 2010, 2012| 21.34| 8.38| 20.41| 0.81|NA |NA | | 1935| 7.3| 163| 2010| 23.68| 9.08| 22.69| 0.70|NA |NA | | 1935| 8.1| 165| 2010| 25.59| 9.84| 24.98| 1.18|NA |NA | | 1935| 8.3| 112| 2010| 28.33| 10.00| 26.70| 1.97|NA |NA | **Score range** (non-Preleo group, in correct items per minute). coding under review) | 8.3| 465| 0.020| 0.826| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 8.3| 464| -0.029| 0.535| |School (ICC) | 8.3| 472| 0.053| | ## For publications The LEEDUCA platform task “Pseudoword reading: three syllables” (codes 1935 and 76; DIS-ESP battery) assesses decoding (sublexical route). The child reads aloud the stimuli shown on the screen and the examiner records each correct response or error. It comprises 12 items. The time limit is 30 seconds. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2010, 2011 and 2012 cohorts it was administered in 16 sessions, from 6 to 8 years of age. The main outcome is the efficiency (correct responses per unit of time). In our data (2021 analyses), internal consistency was α = .92 (N = 637, 12 items). Stability across successive administrations (median interval of 4 months) was ρ = .71 (median of 13 session pairs; range .44–.76). Because the task is timed, α tends to overestimate reliability; stability across administrations is the preferred estimate. Stability across time points was ρ = .43–.80. Against later poor reading comprehension, AUC = .45–.61. ## Pending issues - Extreme value at 7.2 (form 1935), 8.3 (form 1935): the maximum or minimum is more than 2 SD away from P99 or P1. Check in the raw data (possible timing or recording error). - The task has 2 forms; in 0 of 2 comparisons they have different scales. Norms are given by form (see "Forms"). - The persistent difficulty label uses this task: validity against it is circular. - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
